📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 12:48.

Tottenham Hotspur have been handed a potential latest concern over James Maddison's fitness ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash with Sunderland.

The Lilywhites hit the road to face the Black Cats at the Stadium of Light this Sunday, aiming to register their fifth win from their last six Premier League matches.

Spurs' recent resurgence has propelled them into the top half of the Premier League table, as they bounced back from their 1-0 defeat at Leeds United by dispatching Ipswich Town 2-0 on home soil.

Roberto De Zerbi's men got the better of the Tractor Boys despite the absence of Sandro Tonali, who was a last-minute omission from the matchday squad due to illness.

The Italian was filmed being put through his paces with the team in Tuesday's open training session, though, handing Spurs a welcome boost ahead of their trek north.

However, according to Sky Sports News journalist Michael Bridge, Maddison was restricted to indoor work, raising fears of another potential fitness concern for the playmaker.

Sandro Tonali back after missing the win over Ipswich. James Maddison doing indoor work. #THFC https://t.co/EsvY9oqNqb.

Maddison has only made three Premier League starts this season, having spent the majority of the 2025-26 campaign recovering from a serious ACL problem before also picking up a shoulder problem.

The 30-year-old was an unused substitute against Crystal Palace and Leeds earlier this month, and he was taken off in the 64th minute of Saturday's victory over Ipswich.

It is not clear whether Maddison's absence from team training was down to a genuine upcoming injury for the Englishman, or if he is simply being protected ahead of the weekend's fixture.

Nevertheless, for a player who has already missed 73 games for club and country since joining Tottenham from Leicester City in 2023, any minor fitness development could set off alarm bells in Spurs fans' heads.

While Maddison's situation will be closely monitored, Tonali's return from illness is one of two early boosts that Tottenham have received for the trip to Sunderland.

The Black Cats will be unable to call on Kevin Danso this weekend, as the on-loan Tottenham defender is ineligible to face his parent club.

Danso's absence may not have a massive bearing on Regis Le Bris's selection, though, as the Austrian has been an unused substitute in each of Sunderland's last three Premier League games.

Danso started each of the Black Cats' first five top-flight matches of the new season, but he has not played a minute of Premier League football since being sent off against Bournemouth on October 18.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There have been some dark days in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era but this was up there with the very worst of them: the kind of performance that gets a manager sacked, the kind of display that points to a fundamental disconnect, the kind of occasion that leaves you thinking Manchester United are as far away as they have ever been.

When players seem so averse to doing the very basics, such as running, and the club habitually have such trouble attracting the right profiles and personalities, it is hard to escape the feeling that saying goodbye to another manager is going to do little more than paper over the many cracks at Old Trafford.

But, watching this, you had to think Michael Carrick will do well to limp on as far as Sunday, when United face Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

In a recent development, and that was before we had heard the United captain, Bruno Fernandes, appearing to call out the manager’s tactics just a week on from the last show of public dissent from a player, when Lisandro Martínez attacked the Old Trafford board. If only these players were as good at talking on the pitch.

At the final whistle, Carrick walked over to the 700-strong group of United supporters, held up both hands in apology on no fewer than seven occasions and then walked off down the tunnel without looking in the direction of any of his players.

There were shades of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer at Watford in November 2021, when he also held up his hands in apology before being sacked 24 hours later.

In that instance, United fans booed Solskjaer. Carrick at least received some polite applause from the fans, who are a smart bunch and know the club’s problems extend far beyond the man in the dugout. Still, it is always the manager who pays the price. Solskjaer noted he knew at half-time he was toast and Carrick is now under real threat himself – and seemingly at loggerheads with his captain.

Fernandes’s criticism of United’s set-up and approach was cutting and a direct attack on his manager and backroom team. “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man to man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” the United captain stated.

"I think sometimes we have to be more brave under pressure." Captain Bruno Fernandes gives his immediate reaction to Manchester United's heavy 4-1 defeat to Como 🗣️ 🎙️ @LiamMacdevitt 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/8bzmLGkRAX.

It has been revealed that there may be some truth in that, but Carrick’s response felt the most accurate assessment of the lot and will certainly chime with supporters who have long questioned how and why so many United sides, regardless of the manager, reach a point where running, intensity and urgency seem optional. “Whatever tactics you play, if you don’t run, and you don’t run forward, and you don’t run back, you ain’t going to win,” Carrick said.

Carrick has been telling us for weeks that he and his squad are together, that the team are not too far away, that it is all about small margins. He even described Sunday’s 1-1 draw at Leeds as a “fresh start”. But Como blew the lid off any pretence of that being the case. Even by the standards of this season to date, though, what unfolded here in the rain in Lombardy was shocking to witness.

Como, inspired by the outstanding Nico Paz, were every bit as good as United – who have won just two of 11 games this season – were a pitiful mess.

Having conceded after just 47 seconds to Atlético Madrid last week, United were behind after only 118 seconds this time. That in itself told you a lot about these players and this team and it set the tone for what was to follow: a masterclass in incompetence and indifference. There have only been four worse results in United’s European history, although you will struggle to find a poorer performance than this.

Michael Carrick has insisted there is not a “toxic culture” at Manchester United in the wake of scathing criticism from former manager Erik ten Hag of the Old Trafford hierarchy and player power at the club.

The current United manager – who is under pressure after the club’s worst start to a season for 40 years – also believes he has the backing of the United board, despite Ten Hag accusing Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s Ineos regime of a series of “broken promises”.

In an interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag blamed Ratcliffe and his executives for fuelling a “toxic culture” by giving power to players and failing to back him on disciplinary matters relating to Marcus Rashford, Jadon Sancho and other first-teamers.

But Carrick mentioned he had not encountered any toxicity since taking over from Ruben Amorim in January and suggested United’s last two outings, a 1-1 draw against Leeds United and a 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid, underlined the camaraderie in the group.

“Since I came back, the players and the staff have given us everything that they could give,” Carrick stated before Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Cesc Fàbregas’s Como in northern Italy, where he is battling an injury and illness crisis.

“We’ve had some good performances. We’ve had some performances that we want to do better and we can improve on. We’ve made some mistakes.

Sources indicate that “But I have to say, the type of performance put into the weekend and for large parts against Atlético, there’s a lot of togetherness there. There’s a lot of will and determination to do better and wanting to do it for each other, which is key.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Manchester United’s trip to Como in the Champions League. Under normal circumstances, a visit to the idyllic Lombardy city would be a source of thrill and wonder, but Michael Carrick heads into the eye of a literal and proverbial storm at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia with his team desperately hoping to reverse their fortunes.

Absolutely tipping it down in Como, with 64mm of rain forecast before #MUFC kick-off here tomorrow ☔️ https://t.co/WvI3X8dilh.

Two wins – against Ipswich Town and Sabah – in United’s first 10 matches of the season, a public outburst from Lisandro Martínez and accusations of a “toxic culture” at the club have piled pressure on Carrick. And an uninspiring draw at Elland Road on Sunday did little to settle the rising tide of discontent within the United fanbase.

When asked for his team news, the first words that came from the United head coach’s mouth were: “Right, bit of mixed bag to be honest.” That was not a great sign, and Carrick will be without Martínez, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Ayden Heaven, Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu, who are injured, while Leny Yoro serves a suspension following his red card against Atlético Madrid.

Like United, the hosts are without a handful of key players, with Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Assane Diao and Jesus Rodriguez missing from the match-day squad. The abundantly talented Argentine No 10 Nico Paz will feature, however, and he will be keen to showcase his talents in the Champions League.

Como have ascended from Serie B to Europe’s top table in three seasons (and from bankruptcy in nine) under Cesc Fàbregas’ watchful eye. The Spaniard is a minority owner and shareholder of the club, but as head coach he has introduced an incisive, possession-based style of play which contains hints of the managerial greats under whom he played: Arsène Wenger, Pep Guardiola, José Mourinho, Vicente del Bosque, Antonio Conte etc.

Last night, AC Milan watched their former midfielder Franck Kessie help their top four chances and even their Scudetto hopes.

After a 5-1 win at San Siro, things couldn’t have got much better for Milan last night. Yet, somehow, they did. Indeed, the late kick-off on Sunday saw Atalanta host Inter and it seemed that the Nerazzurri were heading for another three points, having gone 4-2 up.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, a brace from Charles De Ketelaere – the second coming to make it 4-3 – and a late penalty from Kessie levelled the scoring and meant Inter stayed within two points of the Rossoneri.

Speaking to DAZN after his late equaliser, Kessie admitted that he still saw the game as a derby, even if he’s no longer a Rossoneri representative, as MilanPress relayed.

“We have great faith in coach Sarri and his staff. The season is still long. Tonight we responded strongly. A heavy penalty at the end? You can score or miss: it went well. For me, it was a small derby against Inter: thank goodness I scored… ”.

Given what it means for the title race, the Diavolo will thank the Ivorian for his contribution and if he plays a part in another successful season, he’ll only be thanked more for it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 12:49, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 12:52.

Anderlecht will be aiming to make it three straight wins in the league stage of the Europa League when they travel to OFI Crete on Thursday night.

The visitors will bring a four-game unbeaten run in all competitions into this match, but Crete will enter the European fixture off the back of a 2-0 loss to Panathinaikos in the Greek Super League.

OFI have a record of two wins and two losses from their four matches in the league stage of this season's Europa League, with six points leaving them in 16th position in the overall table.

The Club started their league phase with a 2-0 win over Hoffenheim before losing back-to-back games in the competition against Rennes and Bayer Leverkusen.

However, Christos Kontis' side posted a 2-0 victory over H. Beer Sheva in their last Europa League game on November 5, so they will be aiming to make it back-to-back wins in the tournament.

OFI are playing in the league stage/group stage of a major European tournament for the first time since the 1995-96 campaign, and this is also the first time that they have ever qualified for this round of the UEFA Cup/Europa League.

The Club have European matches to come against Benfica, Sturm Graz and Lech before the end of the group stage in early 2027.

Anderlecht, meanwhile, have also won two and lost two of their four matches in this season's Europa League league stage, with six points leaving them 15th in the table.

The Belgian club started their league phase with a 2-1 loss to Lyon, before going down 1-0 to Dinamo Zagreb in the middle of October, but they have won their last two matches in the tournament against Jagiellonia and Red Bull Salzburg to move onto six points.

Vitor Bruno's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-0 win over Leuven in the league, with the result leaving them in fifth position in Belgium's top flight.

Anderlecht will face Hoffenheim, Sunderland and Marseille in their three European matches after this one, and it would be a surprise if they were not present in the knockout round.

The Purple and Whites won this competition back in 1982-83, and this is their first Europa League league phase campaign since 2024-25.

OFI Crete form (all competitions):.

Anderlecht form (all competitions):.

Crete will be without the services of Kenan Kodro, Kresimir Krizmanic, Fotis Koutsoupias, Konstantinos Lagoudakis, Emmanouil Chnaris and Nikos Marinakis due to injury problems.

Taxiarchis Fountas has scored five times in 19 appearances this season, and the 31-year-old is set to feature in the final third of the field for the hosts.

Meanwhile, there should also be a position in the side for Thiago Nuss, who has provided seven goal contributions in all competitions for Crete this term.

As for Anderlecht, Ilay Camara and Lucas Hey are out of the match due to injury problems.

Mihajlo Cvetkovic has been in strong form for his Belgian club this season, scoring seven goals and registering two assists in 22 matches, and the 19-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There are also expected to be spots in the final third for Danylo Sikan and Jayden Onia-Seke.

OFI Crete possible starting lineup:.

Lilo; Shielis, Nikolaou, Poungouras; Dickmann, Bouchalakis, Androutsos, Athanasiou; Cantalapiedra, Nuss, Fountas.

Anderlecht possible starting lineup:.

Coosemans; Maamar, Omobamidele, Petrot, Augustinsson; Ambros, Llansana, Stroeykens, Onia-Seke; Sikan, Cvetkovic.

This is a difficult match to call; cases can be made for either side to pick up all three points, but we are expecting a close fixture to end with the points being shared.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Martin O’Neill believes Kieran Tierney is back to his very best and harbours no fears about the defender’s fitness levels ahead of a frantic festive schedule.

Although the Celtic manager substituted Tierney towards the end of Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren, the player started – and finished – both of Scotland’s games in the recent international window, when he was deployed as left centre-half in a back-three formation favoured by fresh international manager Sebastien Pocognoli.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

O’Neill admits this could be an option for Celtic if he chooses to play a system that he once was synonymous with during his first spell in charge at the club.

Industry observers note that “Kieran can play as a centre-half, there’s no doubt about it,” mentioned O’Neill. “He competes better in the air than I ever thought he did.

“It was only when I came back to Celtic that I realised that. He will battle in the air and he’s a reliable defender. If we are ever dropping into a back three, then it wouldn’t be a problem for him.”.

Industry observers note that celtic face a tough upcoming run of games, including travelling to take on second-tier Portuguese club Torreense in the Europa League on Thursday night. Two more away games against Hearts and Dundee quickly follow. The Parkhead side have just one more home match – against St Johnstone – before Christmas. Two other assignments, against Aberdeen and Omonia Nicosia, are away.

O’Neill has already spoken of “manoeuvring” players in the first-team squad to ensure no one is pushed beyond their limits.

According to recent reports, tierney clearly merits the most concern given his injury history. However, he has been quietly putting in the minutes for his club as well as his country in recent weeks. He has played the full 90 minutes of two of Celtic’s last four matches and was only subbed off on Saturday with 20 minutes left against St Mirren with the game already won. O’Neill revealed that he has a crafty tactic for dealing with the player if he begins to look like he might want to come off; he pretends not to notice him. There is no point in the player looking forlornly towards the dugout.

“Tierney played two 90 minutes for Scotland and that made it difficult for him to last the full game against St Mirren,” remarked O'Neill.

According to recent reports, “Internationals take it out of you and he played every second. He played left centre back and that maybe means less running, but those games are tough.

Sources indicate that “Previous to his injury, he was feeling it. But since he’s been back, he’s played a lot of games. Sometimes with Kieran, when you feel as if he’s flagging, you just ignore him. If he’s coming near you, you turn away because you want him to play the games!

“Kieran has done great for me,” he added. "He’s been brilliant, he really has, and he’s getting fitter too. Kieran will be big for us in Europe again. You look at the Besiktas game. Our winning goal late on came from his shot when he was still getting high up the pitch.

Industry observers note that “Kieran has done so well for us and there are signs that he’s back to the Kieran Tierney who got a move to Arsenal. He defends well, he creates goals and he comes up with some too.

“I genuinely couldn’t speak highly enough about Kieran. He’s a great lad too - very popular in the dressing room.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 13:05.

Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne is preparing for an emotional homecoming at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night, though his current spell with Napoli has been clouded by transfer speculation and internal friction.

After winning 19 trophies during a glittering 10-year career at Man City, the 35-year-old playmaker reluctantly left the club at the end of the 2024-25 season when the decision was made to not extend his contract.

De Bruyne subsequently signed for Napoli as a free agent, embarking on a fresh challenge in Italian football, but his debut campaign was struck by injury, starting only 16 matches across all competitions as Napoli surrendered their Serie A crown to Inter Milan.

The Belgium international has since played in all 16 games for Napoli across Serie A and the Champions League this term, chipping in with four goals and two assists while operating in a deeper midfield position under head coach Massimiliano Allegri.

De Bruyne is part of an aging Napoli side that are presently languishing down in eighth place in Serie A and sit 27th in the Champions League standings after losing three of their opening four League Phase games.

Tensions boiled over during Napoli’s heavy 4-1 UCL loss at Porto earlier this month, where teammates had to separate De Bruyne and striker Lorenzo Lucca following an angry on-pitch row.

Sources indicate that "Speaking about the pitch, De Bruyne is the best player this year at Napoli. The point is that the whole team is having difficulties, Naples-based journalist Vincenzo Credendino told BBC Sport.

"We saw that there is a problem, at least between De Bruyne and Lorenzo Lucca. Their acting was very, very clear and I think that in that time, the two of them were wrong.

"On one hand you cannot swear at another team-mate but on the other hand, De Bruyne reproached Lucca without encouraging him, so it was a bad show.".

As De Bruyne enters the twilight years of his career, it has been suggested that the “spark never really ignited” between the midfielder and the Naples outfit, raising uncertainty over his future at the club.

When asked about his future at a press conference ahead of Napoli’s Champions League clash with Man City, De Bruyne said: "Not a lot I can say for the moment. I have played at 100% until now and obviously I am not 20 years old, I am turning 36.

Industry observers note that "There is a lot of things going in my mind but there is not a lot to say. I am playing good football, trying to help the team to do well and it has been a bit of a challenging season with a lot of things happening.".

De Bruyne will soon be entering the final six months of his Napoli contract and will be free to negotiate pre-contract agreements with foreign clubs in January.

De Bruyne has also expressed his annoyance over the backlash he and his family have received following controversial comments made by the player’s wife in September.

His wife Michele reportedly told Belgian magazine NINA about their desire to move back to Belgium, saying "the sooner we get there, the better" as De Bruyne leads a "very restricted life" in Naples.

Addressing the media fallout, De Bruyne replied: "To be honest, I am pretty annoyed because if you read the article, that none of you have read, to understand what she mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that "I was away in Belgium and a lot of noise came and a lot of bad reactions to my wife and family. I saw pictures of my house, I don't think it is OK but it is what it is and some press created this in Italy. I don't know why.

"Nobody knows my life, you will never know. People who work with me are not allowed to say anything but obviously it is something that I take away and think about. It has not been nice for my wife or for my family.".

De Bruyne has since been linked with a sensational Premier League return in January, while Dutch giants PSV Eindhoven are understood to have failed with a €2m (£1.7m) opening offer to sign him in the New Year, with Napoli valuing the midfielder closer to €8m (£6.7m), according to Credendino.

Napoli boss Allegri has interestingly refused to rule out a mid-season departure for De Bruyne, stating on Monday that transfer decisions are "down to the players and who wants to leave" once January arrives.

Meanwhile, De Bruyne has spoken out for the first time since Man City were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial regulations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alfred Johansson insists Motherwell’s latest accounts show the club are trending upwards - with Norway’s Bodo Glimt a key reference point.

The Premiership side have reported a profit of £2.3M, which rises to £3.1M when excluding depreciation and finance costs, for the 2025/26 financial year. A record of £5M was generated from player trading while former manager Jens Berthel Askou achieved a fourth place finish in last term’s top flight.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Current manager Johansson’s work was largely in Scandinavia before travelling to Motherwell. He watched Bodo’s rise from lowly divisions to Champions League competitors and feels that shows what a step-by-step approach can do for a club’s long term aspirations. Former Rosenborg gaffer Johansson said: “I can't really use that to ask for more time in terms of performing but definitely, it's evidence of what the club has been doing for the past 18 months at least, that it’s something that is working.

“So that alignment in the club, that philosophy, and that strategy, like we do things like this, and the connection I feel between people inside here and the offices, that everyone wants to pull together in that direction. That is what gives you output all the time.

In a recent development, “This is a club that the budget is very small compared with some of the teams that we want to compete with. That was the same for Bodo/Glimt 10 years ago. Their budget was so small, they went down to the 2nd division in Norway, now they are playing Champions League. You have to build stone by stone, and that's what Motherwell are trying to do, and that's what I feel every day inside these walls.”.

Recent findings suggest that motherwell’s long-term goals are also set to be boosted by a training base being built at nearby Dalziel Park where they right now undergo preparation for matches. Johansson is keen to see the club build on its ability to grasp marginal gains. He explained: ”You don't have that much time in football nowadays. I get asked in the press conference about patience and everything is related to time.

“That means that you have to make the most out of your time. Maybe before 30 years ago you had to optimise every week. Now you have to optimise every hour in top football. That's down to recovery of players, work with their bodies, and you need facilities to be able to facilitate that work. So that's one part of it.

It has been revealed that “That you need to add the facilities for the players to be able to do the work that's needed to play every few days and with that intensity that. Now I saw that from all the top leagues in Europe, that the Scottish Premiership was the second in the world in explosive accelerations, for instance.

In a recent development, “That's one of the more demanding things that you can put the body through. So you need to be able to react. You need to recover from that between matches and trainings, and so on. So you need the facilities for that. We don't have that much time. Right now we are driving back and forth to Dalziel Park. I could maybe take five minutes in my office with a player or on the pitch talking to a player. All of this is optimising time and I think it's essential today.”.

According to recent reports, dundee boss Steven Pressley spoke last week of the lack of national performance centre in Scotland, like Sweden are building in Johansson’s homeland. He added: “I definitely see the point of that's needed. I mean, Denmark, they've been working also now for some years.

In a recent development, “They have a plan now in place for how to build that centre, Sweden the same. Uh, we know that other countries, they did it 20 years ago, like like the Belgians and the Portuguese FA, they did it. They built a newly introduced facility after the Euros. So, of course, it's there to push things and it's needed.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Celtic’s historic European dream hinges on remaining unbeaten in their next two Europa League ties in Portugal and Cyprus as they seek to build on the win over Besiktas before the international break.

According to recent reports, this, at least, is manager Martin O'Neill's view ahead of Thursday night's clash against Torreense, who have already amassed twice as many points as Celtic. The Portuguese second-tier side might be the most likely source of the win O'Neill feels is required. He has challenged his team to secure four points from the next two away fixtures.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It has been revealed that the 3-2 win over Besiktas earlier this month breathed some life back into the Parkhead club’s European campaign. "It gives us a chance, you know," remarked O'Neill.

Celtic are presently sitting 32nd out of 36 teams in the standings. They will have to break new ground to finish among the top 24 and secure a place in the knockout stage. No team has managed to do so after opening with three defeats in the new European league format.

It has been revealed that after Torreense in Leiria on Thursday Celtic travel to meet Omonia Nicosia in their final European game before Christmas. They play Marseille and Union St. Gilloise early in the latest year.

Recent findings suggest that “You'd have to think that we'd need to get four points in the two games to give ourselves a chance so that you've got two left over, including a home game, which will not be easy," said O'Neill. "It would be nice to carry it into January and still have a chance.

"We've taken enough criticism for not doing well enough in Europe and rightly so," he added. "It's the aim of the football club, it's what we've always remarked." O’Neill recalled a sponsors’ event last week where someone mentioned the manner of the Champions League qualifying exit. “Sometimes you feel as if we've never really got over the LASK thing,” he said.

Although much is at stake, O’Neill is still confident that bit-part players to date such as Oliver Sorensen and Joel van den Berg can play a part in the European effort.

Recent findings suggest that both were signed on the last day of the summer transfer window and were included in the European squad. Sorensen has failed to make an impression despite starting the opening two Europa League defeats against Ferencvaros and Benfica while Van den Berg has been sidelined with an ankle injury.

It has been revealed that the Dutch midfielder made his belated debut as a substitute in Saturday’s 4-1 win over St Mirren. Sorensen, meanwhile, has not featured in the last two matchday squads due to a family bereavement. Celtic face a period where auxiliary players will be required to step up.

“This is a chance, with a bit of luck, for the likes of Sorensen and Van den Berg,” noted O’Neill. He challenged Van den Berg to kick on following his cameo at the weekend. He hopes Sorensen, too, can begin to nail down a regular place in the side.

"He has, by his own admission, found it difficult,” said the manager “I think that he also arrived late as well too, trying to get to know people, trying to get his position, trying to get up to speed with what we do.

It has been revealed that "And whatever we do, I bet you it'll be something really different to what he was doing at Parma. But now it would be up to him.”.

Viljami Sinisalo has been waiting for his turn back in goal. O’Neill still hasn't made up mind about who will stay at No. 1.

Sam Johnstone is clearly in possession of the gloves at present even if it would not be a surprise if Sinisalo is given a match before long, perhaps as soon as Thursday. “There’s still good competition,” noted the manager. “Viljami wants to be the keeper here, which is great.

Sources indicate that “He will play again and at some stage you have to make you’re mind up who will stay as no.1. I don’t think there’s a phenomenal amount between them at this stage.”.

Breaking: These gaps in weather data affect forecasts everywhere: plugging them is not charity

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (958 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Observations from data-scarce regions, such as low-lying island Tuvalu in the South Pacific, are crucial to weather forecasts, early warning systems and climate-information services elsewhere.
  • Recent findings suggest that when I talk about collecting essential weather and climate data in countries with limited resources, many take it to mean that wealthier countries, institutions and firms should ‘help poorer ones’.
  • It has been revealed that that’s the resounding conclusion of a report published this month by The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) in collaboration with the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Observations from data-scarce regions, such as low-lying island Tuvalu in the South Pacific, are crucial to weather forecasts, early warning systems and climate-information services elsewhere. Credit: Mario Tama/Getty.

Recent findings suggest that when I talk about collecting essential weather and climate data in countries with limited resources, many take it to mean that wealthier countries, institutions and firms should ‘help poorer ones’. But as a development and climate-finance executive, I know that this is an investment rather than an act of charity. Science proves it: better forecasts at home rely on observations abroad.

It has been revealed that that’s the resounding conclusion of a report published this month by The European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) in collaboration with the World Meteorological Organization (WMO). The report was commissioned by the Systematic Observations Financing Facility (SOFF), a United Nations fund dedicated to basic weather and climate data around the world, of which I am a director.

Its aim was to establish the benefits of filling gaps in the WMO’s Global Basic Observing Network (GBON), which defines member nations’ mandatory weather-station coverage. To comply, each country must have a land station every 200 kilometres, as well as a weather balloon every 500 kilometres over land and every 1,000 kilometres over sea to collect data on essential variables (such as temperature, pressure, humidity and wind).

Global climate body fights for survival: why the IPCC must be saved.

Global climate body fights for survival: why the IPCC must be saved.

Sources indicate that but agreeing on standards and sites is not the same as having the economic means to implement them. Since 2023, GBON stations have been required to share their data. Yet, about 90% of weather data from low-income countries and small island nations are not being shared. Some data are not even collected because many stations are missing, stopped working or cannot transmit their measurements.

These gaps don’t just impede local forecasts, they affect regional and global projections too. Daily weather data feed into increasingly sophisticated computer models that predict how weather systems around the world evolve.

According to recent reports, think of a weather forecast as a photograph. It is made up of millions of pixels, each contributing a small piece of information. Weather forecasting is more complex, but the analogy helps to explain the problem: if too many ‘pixels’ are missing, the global picture is blurry or incomplete. And for forecasts, some ‘pixels’, or observations, are more valuable than others. Plugging gaps in data-scarce regions is the best way to improve forecasts everywhere.

It is also a matter of justice: on average, a seven-day temperature forecast in a high-income country is as accurate as a one-day forecast in a low-income country (M. Linsenmeier and J. G. Shrader Nature Commun. 17, 10792; 2026).

According to recent reports, the results of the ECMWF simulations are striking. Better coverage in low-income countries and small island states can cut uncertainty in 12-hour local forecasts by more than 30% in parts of Africa and by up to 20% across the Pacific.

Sources indicate that extra data in all countries eligible for development assistance and small island nations would improve the accuracy of temperature and wind forecasts up to six or seven days ahead in the tropics, home to some 40% of the world’s population, and in the Northern Hemisphere’s mid-latitudes, where much of Europe, North America and northern Asia sit. This would help with, for example, aviation and maritime operations, planning of agricultural activities, water management and preparations for severe weather.

Disparity in countries’ capacity to finance weather observations is striking. To quantify the inequality, SOFF developed an indicator comparing countries’ gross dom-estic product (GDP) with the geographical area for which they are mandated to provide observations, including marine exclusive economic zones. For example, although it is a small country, Switzerland has a larger budget than does Tuvalu, a Pacific island nation spread across an immense ocean area (Switzerland’s GDP is around 300,000 times larger per square kilometre). Yet both countries contribute to and benefit from the same global observing system.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Raith Rovers have been charged by the Scottish Football Association over a social media post mocking Dunfermline Athletic manager Neil Lennon in the aftermath of the Fife derby.

Following the 0-0 draw at Stark's Park on November 6, Lennon made a pinching gesture with his thumb and forefinger towards rival supporters which was widely interpreted as a jibe calling Raith Rovers a "small club".

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Recent findings suggest that shortly after the final whistle, Raith's official X account shared a photo of Lennon making the gesture alongside the caption, "How big is your penis, Neil?". The club deleted the post 52 minutes later after it went viral.

The SFA compliance officer has now issued the Kirkcaldy outfit with a notice of complaint relating to a breach of Disciplinary Rule 73, which reads: "No recognised football body, club, official, Team Official or other member of Team Staff, player, match official or other person under the jurisdiction of the Scottish FA shall in an interview, a ‘blog’ on the internet, on a social networking or micro-blogging site, or in any other manner calculated or likely to lead to publicity, make comment(s) of a discriminatory or offensive nature based on, but not limited to, race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation or disability, or that endorse or encourage foul play or violent Conduct or are otherwise offensive.

"There shall be a presumption that any material published in such a manner was published in the name of and/or with the authority of the person or body bearing to have published the material.".

Sanctions typically start at a £500 lower-end fine and rise up to a £5,000 top-end fine.

Speaking about the incident last week, Lennon described the episode as "embarrassing for them", referring to Raith, adding; "“You know, that’s like an official club Twitter account, which is embarrassing. I’ll say no more than that.”.

Industry observers note that raith are scheduled to face a Hampden disciplinary hearing on December 17. This falls just over a week before the two sides meet again at East End Park on Boxing Day.

The game finally settled down in the final 20 minutes, and Crawley managed to see the game out for a valuable point, which sees the Reds level on points with Rotherham in 23rd, with a game in hand.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 13:08.
  • Liverpool have confirmed their 22-man travelling squad for Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge at the Jan Breydel Stadion.
  • The Reds are going in search of their fourth win from five continental matches in Belgium, having overcome Atletico Madrid, Villarreal and LASK Linz before a 3-2 loss at Fenerbahce last time out.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 24 Nov 2026 13:08.

Liverpool have confirmed their 22-man travelling squad for Wednesday's Champions League clash with Club Brugge at the Jan Breydel Stadion.

The Reds are going in search of their fourth win from five continental matches in Belgium, having overcome Atletico Madrid, Villarreal and LASK Linz before a 3-2 loss at Fenerbahce last time out.

Andoni Iraola's men have responded to that setback with back-to-back Premier League wins, though, following up a 3-1 triumph at Crystal Palace with a 4-0 battering of Manchester United on Sunday.

Teenage starlet Rio Ngumoha stole the show against the Red Devils in the absence of Cody Gakpo, who was an unexpected absentee from Sunday's matchday squad due to a calf injury.

Iraola revealed that Gakpo suffered his injury while on international duty with the Netherlands, and the attacker has not been included in the travelling party for Wednesday's game.

Gakpo's problem is not believed to be serious, though, and there is a chance that he will be fit to return for the weekend's Merseyside derby with Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

As well as Gakpo, compatriot Ryan Gravenberch will also miss Liverpool's trip to Brugge, as the midfielder continues his recuperation from a small heel fracture.

After the weekend's win over Man Utd, Iraola expressed hope that Gravenberch would be fit for the Champions League clash, having returned to training while carefully managing his pain.

However, the Netherlands international will now miss a fourth consecutive game for Liverpool, and he is still waiting for his first minutes of November, having also been an unused substitute against Arsenal.

Gravenberch and Gakpo are two of five Liverpool absentees against Club Brugge, as Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley (both knee) have not made the cut either.

The rest of Liverpool's squad is as expected, and alongside Ngumoha, five other Kirkby youngsters could earn opportunities to impress at the Jan Breydel Stadion.

Nineteen-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni could make his fourth consecutive start in the Champions League after appearing from the off against LASK, Villarreal and Fenerbahce, scoring against the latter.

Twenty-two-year-old James McConnell is also involved, but the midfielder has been restricted to just one nine-minute cameo in the UCL against Villarreal so far.

Wide man Luke Chambers, meanwhile, was given five minutes off the bench against LASK, but he has not made a single Premier League matchday squad this season.

Finally, attacking duo Lewis Koumas and Jayden Danns could earn valuable European minutes; the latter is yet to make a competitive appearance for Liverpool under Iraola.

Rangers half-time surgery sparks second half tempest to subdue Ibrox anxiety

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (818 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Scotsman

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are evenings when tactical blueprints dissolve into sheer, unscripted theatre, and for 45 minutes at a rain-soaked Ibrox, it appeared as though Derek McInnes’ best-laid plans had conspired against his own side.
  • In testing conditions, both sides abandoned any pretence of caution to serve up a thrilling second half that was in stark contrast to the opening 45 minutes, which offered little beyond frustration and creeping anxiety for the Rangers manager.
  • Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are evenings when tactical blueprints dissolve into sheer, unscripted theatre, and for 45 minutes at a rain-soaked Ibrox, it appeared as though Derek McInnes’ best-laid plans had conspired against his own side. Yet by the time a frenetic second half had run its course, Rangers had conjured an epic turnaround to claim a breathless 3–2 victory over Aberdeen that saw them move within a point of idle Premiership leaders Celtic.

In testing conditions, both sides abandoned any pretence of caution to serve up a thrilling second half that was in stark contrast to the opening 45 minutes, which offered little beyond frustration and creeping anxiety for the Rangers manager.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Facing the club where he spent eight formative years in the dugout, McInnes had tinkered with his starting formation, handing Ben Godfrey a first start since July 31st as part of a three-man defence designed to counter their opponents narrow, winger-less system, However, the hosts looked entirely disjointed.

Rangers, playing their first home match in a full month following an unusual sequence of five consecutive away fixtures, began on the front foot. However, despite Dan Neil squandering a glorious opportunity from six yards inside the opening 60 seconds, his rebound subsequently struck off teammate Ryan Naderi, the home side struggled to establish rhythm or coherence.

Aberdeen, aiming to build on their first win under newly introduced head coach Mario Frick at the weekend, sensed vulnerability and grew steadily in conviction. Organised in a compact 4-3-1-2 shape, the visitors frustrated Rangers before delivering a clinical blow on the half-hour mark. Brad Lyons capitalised on Rangers’ hesitation from a corner to produce a diving header that was hooked off the line by Nico Raskin. However, after VAR intervened, the ball was adjudged to have crossed the line and referee John Beaton awarded the goal, sparking wild celebrations scenes in the away end.

Worse almost followed for the hosts. Only profligacy in front of goal, most notably from Moroccan striker Ayoub Mouloua, who twice spurned clear openings before the interval, prevented the Dons from carrying a more commanding lead into the break as the Rangers supporters made their dissatisfaction known.

If the first half belonged to Aberdeen’s disciplined industry, the opening 12 minutes of the second belonged to Rangers’ ruthless efficiency. McInnes wasted little time in rectifying his questionable team selection, executing a bold triple substitution at half-time that saw Kim Min-su, Tuur Rommens and Findlay Curtis replace Kevin Kelsy, Godfrey, and Badredine Bouanani.

Industry observers note that the transformation was instantaneous. Within 60 seconds of the restart, Min-su tested Aberdeen goalkeeper Marius Müller with a dipping shot. Müller could only parry the ball directly into the path of Ryan Naderi, who gleefully dispatched the rebound from close range to restore parity.

Industry observers note that before Aberdeen could draw breath, Ibrox erupted once more. Just 64 seconds after the equaliser, Naderi turned provider, threading an incisive pass into Djeidi Gassama. Outpacing his man, the winger kept his composure to drill a low finish across Müller into the far corner. In barely a minute, a packed stadium that had been growing increasingly restless was suddenly alive again.

It has been revealed that rangers’ third arrived in the 56th minute via a devastating counter-attack. Min-su, whose introduction had injected vital urgency into the hosts' attacking play, won possession deep inside his own half and drove up field before releasing Gassama. Cutting the ball neatly across the penalty area, the Mauritanian international teed up Raskin, who coolly side-footed low across Müller to establish a seemingly decisive 3-1 advantage.

Industry observers note that aberdeen, however, refused to crumble. Barely a minute after Raskin’s goal, Alexander Briedl drifted inside from the left flank and slipped a weighted pass into the path of Findlay Marshall. The youngster met it cleanly, sending a crisp drive crashing in off the post to reduce the deficit and reignite a pulsating contest.

Industry observers note that what followed was a nerve-shredding final half-hour punctuated by transitions and agonising near-misses. Aberdeen’s Nesta Guinness-Walker endured frustration when his late penalty appeal was waved away. In between, Marshall came within inches of securing a share of the spoils, dragging a left-footed effort agonisingly wide of Pandur's post in the closing stages after the Croatian had made a spectacular save to deny Nicky Devlin from a corner at his front post.

In a recent development, if Scottish football occasionally stands accused of predictability, nobody among the 50,738 crowd could reasonably complain of short measure. Rangers survived, although not without making their supporters endure another uncomfortable finale as they took advantage of their game in hand to move closer to keeper their title challenge firmly on track.

Vito Mannone - 8.5: The Italian shot stopper pulled off a great stop low down to his left on 25 minutes to keep the score at 0-0. Pemi Aderoju – 7.5: His hold up play was second to none and was effective at bringing others into the game.

Lewis Richards – 6: Playing in the wing back role, Richards defended well when required and played a number of decent balls into the channel for Orsi to run onto.

Jonny Russell – 6.5: Moving into the back three from wing-back he didn’t look out of place and dealt with Barnet’s number fast and physical nine Jack Maskell extremely well.

Dylan Morgan – 7: Picked up the ball in some great central positions and used his neat footwork to bypass the Barnet players and move the ball into space.

Hibs head coach Marink Reedijk was delighted with his team’s display as they overcame Dundee 2-1 to claim a first home league win in nearly eight months.

The Leith side struck twice in the space of three minutes just before half-time with Martin Boyle converting from the penalty spot and Nicky Cadden producing a stunning finish.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Dundee – hurting from Saturday’s 8-0 hammering by Hearts – put up a fight after the interval and Joe Wright’s strike gave them hope of a comeback.

But Hibs held on to secure their first league victory in front of their own supporters since beating Kilmarnock on April 4.

Reedijk noted: “It’s always nice to win, it’s a good one again in order to make sure we get confirmation that if we show our identity about intensity, aggression and proactivity and are brave, that anything can happen here.

“I hope we get another three points next match and that we go again in a way that we do the things we are good at and what our identity and what we stand for is.

“The next match against Motherwell is not at home, I know, but there will be a match at home against Rangers, where this can also come to life again. But that is far away.

“First things first, Saturday lies another challenge.”.

Reedijk was also pleased to see Cadden rack up a stunning strike – the wing-back finding the net in only his second start of the season.

The effort came from a cleverly worked corner routine, with Hibs having already threatened from a similar set-piece earlier in the match.

Reedijk also singled out assistant coach Rogier Molhoek for praise for devising the short corner routines.

In a recent development, he added: “It was a beautiful goal, wasn’t it? It was one when he left the foot, I was like, ‘ooh, he hits it well and you saw the angle of the ball’.

In a recent development, “We try to use every quality we have in order to make it difficult for opponents to see what we are doing in the beginning. Also we look at their organisation and if their organisation allows us to attack certain spaces, we try to do this.

Recent findings suggest that “This is the job of Rogier, he always makes routines – and also with crazy names. You will never know these names because sometimes it’s not polite.”.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley was encouraged by his side’s response to the humiliation against Hearts despite his team falling to a third consecutive league loss.

It has been revealed that he said: “Both teams are a bit fragile and there was a lot of trepidation in the game but the one thing about us we got a degree of pride back. It’s not the result but a little bit of stability and we highlighted a lot of courage.

“We wanted to give ourselves a foundation to build from and we gave ourselves that.

“We were much more cohesive in the second half and when you suffer the defeat we suffered on Saturday and you come here and you find yourself 2-0 down at half-time, it asks a lot of questions of you as a group and I thought they responded brilliantly.

“They revealed courage and spirit and it’s not been easy because there’s a fragility about us. We responded in the proper manner.”.

'That was tough' - Crawley Town boss gives honest assessment of stalemate with high-flying Barnet

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The stalemate made it eight points in four games in charge for Blackwell as Reds closed the gap on safety in League Two.
  • Reds had chances in the first half but second-placed Barnet put on the pressure in the second half but a mixture of solid defending and an inspired Vito Mannone kept the visitors at bay.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The stalemate made it eight points in four games in charge for Blackwell as Reds closed the gap on safety in League Two.

Reds had chances in the first half but second-placed Barnet put on the pressure in the second half but a mixture of solid defending and an inspired Vito Mannone kept the visitors at bay.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Industry observers note that “Wow, bloody hell, that was tough”, noted Blackwell. "It's a very direct game, that's for sure, and they played it quite well, so I'm really pleased with the way the players dealt with it.

Industry observers note that “They're an experienced side and we had a lot of youngsters again today, so all credit to them. "I thought Ben Heneghan, once again, at the centre of the back three has done really well.

Recent findings suggest that “It's a typical system to play against and I can see why they're high up in the league, it's causing teams problems. But I think overall, you know, Vito's not had many saves to make it, has he?.”.

It has been revealed that blackwell was pleased with how his reduced the amount of gilt-edged chances Dean Brennan’s side had. “There wasn't clear-cut chances,” he stated. “It's a system that I've not seen for a long time, but it just meant we had to be focused all the time, they do things quickly, they're long throws, long balls, the keeper kicks it from box to box.

Industry observers note that “They know that the major nine is going to flick it on and they make runners in behind and your midfield and your centre-halves have to stay with runners. So it was a disciplined performance tonight against a team, like I say, who play a very direct style, but are good at what they do.”.

And the former Leeds boss highlighted that despite the gap in league positions, there was not much in quality between the two sides.

Blackwell said: “You look at it, it was top versus bottom, but you wouldn't have known. I don't think you'd have known.

“Yes, they put us under a bit of pressure towards the end and exactly what a team at the top, full of confidence, you'd expect them to do that. But we were resilient and it's a difficult one for me to express the game other than it was concentration, do your job, throw your body in the way when required and stand up to a team that can bully you if you allow them to. Like I said, you know, Pemi [Aderoju] and Osman [Kamara] and Duke [Stephen Duke-McKenna, they've got a lot of youngsters we have and you're going to learn a lot from that.

“I hope they learn a lot. But what I'm pleased about is the resilience.”.

And Blackwell added: “The question was about people coming to Crawley and getting easy points and I think we put a statement down certainly today that if you want to come to Crawley, you're going to have to earn your points if you want to work away with anything.

“So, once again, it's all credit to the players.”.

Aston Villa's Champions League clash with Galatasaray plunged into chaos as Turkish police hunt for a fugitive LION spotted 10 miles from the stadium

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:24 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:09 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.
  • In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:24 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 18:09 EST, 23 November 2026.

A lion has been spotted about ten miles from the stadium where Aston Villa are due to face Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In a bizarre development, Turkish security and wildlife personnel were on Monday searching for the animal​, believed to be roaming loose ‌in woodland north of Istanbul.

Around 70 people, including police and other emergency personnel, have been involved in the search, with seven drones deployed. The animal was first sighted in Istanbul's Sariyer district, which is also where Galatasaray's RAMS Park is located.

According to local reports, personnel at a police station in ​the Zekeriyakoy area, north of the ​European side of Istanbul, reported seeing 'an animal ⁠resembling a lion' on surveillance cameras at ​around 9pm local time on Sunday (6pm GMT).

Sources indicate that extensive security measures have been put in place around the forested area where the animal is believed to be located and nearby villas. Access to and from the area is being controlled, while residents have been warned to remain cautious.

'The area where the lion is located has been identified, and every effort is being made to capture it alive,' the Istanbul Governor's Office remarked in a statement.

A lion has been spotted 10 miles from where Aston Villa are set to play in the Champions League on Tuesday.

The Istanbul Governor's Office remarked 'every effort' is being made to capture the lion alive.

Recent findings suggest that reaction to the lion's escape bordered on the surreal, with one outlet interviewing a person in a lion suit, wearing a Galatasaray shirt, about it. Galatasaray are nicknamed the Lions while Villa have a lion on their badge.

In a recent development, gala defender Abdulkerim Bardakci was even asked about the matter, and replied: 'I want to say something because the whole country is talking about this right now. There's only one lion I keep at home, and that's my son.'.

Daily Mail Sport has contacted UEFA for an revision.

There were even suggestions in Turkey that Villa had cancelled their training session at RAMS Park because of the lion, but Villa did their preparation at Bodymoor Heath for a very different reason – the state of the RAMS Park pitch.

European football chiefs are confident the playing surface will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Sources indicate that yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries. 'We have to think that if there was a risk of injury, we wouldn't be playing on it,' he remarked. 'The pitch will be better or worse, for both teams.'.

According to recent reports, villa defender Ian Maatsen noted: 'We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.'.

Sources indicate that galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: 'It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.'.

Villa, who have been followed abroad by Prince William this season, will take on Galatasaray.

Aston Villa shocked Europe by marching straight into the last 16 in the Champions League two seasons ago but a win over Galatasaray will put them on course to repeat it.

Unai Emery’s side have nine points from a possible 12 in the league phase and victory in Istanbul will give them one foot in the knockout rounds.

Daily Mail Sport looks at what Villa can expect from one of the toughest tests on the European calendar.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa after conducting thorough inspections of the playing surface at RAMS Park.

The Turkish giants have commissioned intensive work on the pitch and moved their most recent league game, against Samsunspor, to the stadium of rivals Istanbul Basaksehir.

Yet it is thought conditions will be some way from perfect and though Villa boss Unai Emery played it down, he will be anxious about injuries.

Villa defender Ian Maatsen stated: ‘We don't know anything about the pitch. They say it's in a little bit of a bad condition but that's no excuse. We have to see how the pitch is. We are ready.’.

Recent findings suggest that galatasaray coach Okan Buruk added: ‘It was dug up again, another hybrid treatment was applied, and seeds were planted. There is also sand mixed into the pitch to help.’.

Recent findings suggest that villa are back in their happy place. This city hosted their 3-0 win over Freiburg in the Europa League Final last May, though that game happened at Tupras Stadium, home of Besiktas.

According to recent reports, repeat that result here and Villa will be eyeing a top-eight finish – which they also achieved two years ago. That would allow them to skip the play-off round early next year and head straight into the last 16.

European football chiefs are confident Galatasaray’s pitch will pose no risk to Aston Villa (Source: X/Forza Cimbom).

Will Garnacho’s chance ever come?

Five months into his loan spell from Chelsea, Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa.

Recent findings suggest that when the Argentine moved to Villa Park, it was suggested that turning the temporary move into a £43million permanent deal would be a relative formality. Right now, that feels nearly impossible. Garnacho has featured for only 95 minutes this term and if Emery really did want the 22-year-old last summer, he has a funny way of showing it.

Indeed, Daily Mail Sport understands that even during Garnacho’s early days at the club, some Villa players were starting to wonder whether he would ever play regularly for Emery.

What next? There is believed to be no recall clause in the loan deal with Chelsea yet as Garnacho has only represented Villa this term, the clubs could agree to cancel the arrangement in January.

It has been revealed that born in Madrid, Garnacho was part of the youth system at Atletico before joining Manchester United. With four Argentines in the Atletico squad, plus another in boss Diego Simeone, that might be worth keeping an eye on.

According to recent reports, yet it is thought that neither Galatasaray nor Fenerbahce, who were monitoring Garnacho last summer, are in the market for a high-wage signing in January. That would close off one potential escape route.

Thanks to the sales of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans that brought in nearly £200million, Villa were able to spend heavily in the summer.

In a recent development, to invest again in the winter, they will probably need to attract offers for some fringe players. As well as Garnacho, Tammy Abraham and Lamare Bogarde have been overlooked by Emery recently. Abraham has fallen behind Brian Madjo in the pecking order, though the 17-year-old was not included in the Champions League squad, while Bogarde’s only starts have been in the Carabao Cup, which is always low on Emery’s priority list. Selling Bogarde would also deliver pure profit – crucial for a club forever fighting to stay in line with Premier League and UEFA spending rules.

There were always going to be bumps in the road this season for Villa, and there will likely be more. In last Saturday’s dispiriting 0-0 draw with Sunderland, there were only two players – Emi Buendia and Pau Torres – in the starting XI who were also in the line-up for the Europa League Final. Replacing the six who departed will take time.

In their commendable attempts to bring down the average age of the squad, Villa find themselves with a surplus of attackers but no midfield controller since the departure of Tielemans, and they also look vulnerable in central defence.

Tyrone Mings turns 34 in March and Victor Lindelof was 32 in July while Taylor Harwood-Bellis must find his feet swiftly in one of the most demanding competitions in the world. It is tough without Konsa.

Sources indicate that elsewhere, there are possibly too many options. George Hemmings and then Alysson have forced their way into the side at different times this season, meaning fewer opportunities for Ibrahim Mbaye, who cost nearly £50million from Paris Saint-Germain last summer. Johan Manzambi has played regularly and with John McGinn and Buendia also in the mix, a player like Garnacho has a near-impossible task to convince Emery.

Alejandro Garnacho is still waiting for his first competitive start for Aston Villa - five months after joining from Chelsea.

Scouts from across Europe have been watching Galatasaray’s matches this season and Aleksey Batrakov is usually the reason why.

The 21-year-old Russian playmaker has six goals – including four in the Champions League – and four assists since his £21million move from Lokomotiv Moscow and is one of the breakout stars of the world game.

He caught the eye of Paris Saint-Germain while playing for Lokomotiv and Barcelona boss Hansi Flick has praised him.

The last Russian to play in the Premier League was Pavel Pogrebnyak, whose last game for Reading was against West Ham in May 2013.

Given the current geopolitical situation, Pogrebnyak will surely hold that record for some time to come.

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 13:22, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:24.

Ferencvaros will be aiming to make it five wins in the league stage of the 2026-27 Europa League when they welcome Celje to Budapest on Thursday night.

The Greens will enter this match off the back of a 3-1 loss to Gyor in the league, while Celje recorded a 2-0 victory over Grosuplje in their last domestic game on November 22.

Ferencvaros have been excellent in this season's Europa League, beating Celtic, Viktoria Plzen, Torreense and AC Milan in the league stage of the tournament, with 12 points leaving them in third position in the table, level on points with the top two Benfica and Bournemouth.

Balazs Borbely's side were 2-0 winners over Milan in their last European match, which was a statement result, but their six-game winning run in all competitions came to an end on November 21 when they were overcome by Gyor in Hungary's top flight.

Ferencvaros reached the last-16 stage of the 2025-26 Europa League, ultimately losing to Braga, and they have been regulars in the knockout round of the competition of late.

It would be a shock if the Hungarian team were unable to progress to the knockout stage of this season's tournament given their strong position in the table.

Ferencvaros will take on Lech, Juventus and Hoffenheim in their final three games in the league stage of this season's Europa League.

Celje, meanwhile, have a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in this season's competition, with four points leaving them down in 25th spot in the table.

The Yellow and Blues are opened their campaign with back-to-back losses to Bayer Leverkusen and Omonia before claiming a point in a 2-2 draw with Red Bull Salzburg.

Zoran Zeljkovic's side then recorded a 3-2 victory over Sturm Graz in their last European fixture, and Celje have actually won their last five matches in all competitions.

The Yellow and Blues have not been beaten since the 3-0 reverse to Omonia in the middle of October, so they will enter Thursday's match in strong form.

Celje played in the Conference League last season, reaching the last-16 stage of the tournament before going down 4-2 on aggregate to AEK Athens.

Ferencvaros form (all competitions):.

Ferencvaros will be missing Bence Otvos on Thursday through injury, while Bamidele Yusuf is suspended for the European fixture with Celje.

Kristoffer Zachariassen has been in excellent form this season, scoring 11 goals and registering nine assists in 25 appearances, and the 32-year-old will again be in the side.

Meanwhile, there should also be a spot through the middle for Lenny Joseph, who has six goals and three assists in 18 appearances during the current campaign.

As for Celje, no injuries have been reported ahead of the contest.

Svit Seslar has been the team's standout player this season from an attacking point of view, scoring 11 goals and registering two assists in 24 appearances, and the 24-year-old is set to start.

There is also expected to be a position through the middle for Armandas Kucys, who has netted five times for Celje during the 2026-27 campaign.

Dibusz; Osvath, Raemaekers, Gomez, Nagy; Madarasz, Maiga; Zachariassen, Bero, Birmancevic; Joseph.

Leban; Ivansek, Bejger, Tutyskinas, Avdyli; Zabukovnik; Dukuly, Seslar, Kvesic, Verbic; Kucys.

Derek McInnes airs his Rangers frustrations and ‘biggest takeaway’ as new Aberdeen boss makes ‘beatable’ claim

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Derek McInnes has warned his Rangers side they must learn to control games more efficiently for longer periods if they are to sustain their Scottish Premiership title challenge this season.
  • The Ibrox manager praised the resilience of his players after they managed to overturn a half-time deficit to beat a revitalised Aberdeen 3-2 in a thrilling contest, courtesy of a decisive ten-minute goal blitz early in the second half.
  • Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Derek McInnes has warned his Rangers side they must learn to control games more efficiently for longer periods if they are to sustain their Scottish Premiership title challenge this season.

The Ibrox manager praised the resilience of his players after they managed to overturn a half-time deficit to beat a revitalised Aberdeen 3-2 in a thrilling contest, courtesy of a decisive ten-minute goal blitz early in the second half.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

However, McInnes was frustrated that Rangers allowed their opponents back quickly into the contest after establishing a seemingly unassailable cushion, which left them clinging on during an increasingly anxious finale.

Ryan Naderi, Djeidi Gassama and Nico Raskin turned the game around, before Findlay Marshall's immediate response ensured the Dons went down fighting.

Despite the satisfaction of extending their unbeaten run to 14 matches, McInnes was unhappy with the manner in which his team surrendered control, insisting his players put unnecessary pressure on themselves.

“Delighted we've got the job done. Great win for us in the end,” he remarked. “Disappointed we've allowed ourselves to be hanging on at the end rather than controlling the game. The question was being asked of us at half-time. We were in a difficult spot. We were having to dig it deep and you find out about your players in these sort of situations. It's good to know that we have dug that result out.

“We need to recognise that we need to be better for longer periods, particularly at Ibrox. By conceding the second goal, we should still stay on the job, but with too many negative passes, too many backwards passes, we need to own that a wee bit.

"The biggest takeaway for me tonight is my players had to dig deep. We were in a tough spot at half-time, 50,000, 1-0 down at home to Aberdeen. That's not an easy place to be. It's alright for me to try and address it tactically, having a go at half-time or whatever, but they've still got to go and deliver, and they delivered a big performance.”.

McInnes had initially opted for a system designed to exploit the spaces around Aberdeen's front two, with Gassama and Badredine Bouanani providing width on both flanks. However, he conceded that his side had not been productive enough despite repeatedly getting into promising positions in the final third before a triple half-time substitution altered the formation to provide greater control in central areas.

“I thought the subs helped us and I thought for 20 minutes we were outstanding,” McInnes added. “We showed the speed, the intensity, the quality, the intelligence. We blew them away.”.

New Aberdeen head coach Mario Frick was left frustrated by his side’s collapse immediately after half-time, but felt they had shown enough to suggest Rangers were there for the taking.

In a recent development, “I am disappointed with the five or six minutes after half-time. That hurts,” he stated. “We saw a good performance, Rangers were beatable tonight. We need more time. We have to improve. We have to talk about those ten minutes.

“After 3-1 down we came back and we believed in ourselves. We deserved the equaliser. We came to win and we are disappointed to go back with zero points. I see a lot of positives things.”.

Charalampos Kostoulas is convinced Stefanos Tzimas has the mentality to come back stronger as Brighton's Greek connection prepares for a potential reunion on the pitch.

The two forwards arrived at the Amex in 2025, with Brighton investing a combined total of around £50m in the pair of young talents from Greece.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Tzimas signed from FC Nurnberg in January 2025 for a reported £20.8m, before joining up with the Seagulls that summer and Kostoulas followed from Olympiacos, signing in June for a reported £29.8m.

Sources indicate that but their hopes of developing a partnership have been interrupted by injury. Tzimas suffered a serious ACL injury during Brighton's 4-3 defeat by Aston Villa last December, going down while pressing defender Pau Torres after 24 minutes.

The 20-year-old has been sidelined for almost a year. He made nine appearances for Brighton before the injury, scoring once and providing one assist.

Kostoulas - who has impressed this term with five goals and four assists - is delighted to see his compatriot make progress following his return to full training.

"I'm really happy for him," he told Sussex World. "It was a long time, but he was always really clear in his mind.

“He was looking at every day as one day closer to his comeback. He's really good. He has a really good mindset and I have big trust in him.

The pair have both featured in the same Brighton match, their competitive debuts in the 6-0 Carabao Cup win at Oxford United in August 2025.

However, they have yet to share the pitch: Tzimas was substituted in the 77th minute and Kostoulas came on a minute later.

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has been encouraged by Tzimas' return to first-team training, but is keen not to rush him back.

Industry observers note that speaking ahead of the 2-0 loss at Hull City, Hurzeler noted: "He's a great personality, and that's also shown by his teammates. Everyone was happy for him.

“Everyone really appreciates that he fought that hard for this comeback.

It has been revealed that "Now, of course, we have to be patient. It won't be that he will immediately be an option for us. He was out for a long time, so we need to give him time.".

Tzimas was pictured in full training yesterday and there’s a slim chance he could be included in Thursday night’s Uefa Conference League matchday squad matchday squad to face Romanian league leaders Craiova at the Amex Stadium.

Keep an eye on the Sussex World website for further updates later today.

For Kostoulas, the prospect of finally playing alongside his fellow Greek in is an exciting one.

Asked what it would mean to have two Greek forwards representing Brighton, he added with a smile: "Also, two offensive players!".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rangers produced a quickfire second-half comeback to beat Aberdeen 3-2 at Ibrox and move to within a point of Scottish Premiership leaders Celtic on Tuesday night.
